name: Ticketbud
description: Ticketbud is an event ticketing and registration platform for building event pages, selling tickets, managing orders and attendees, checking guests in and connecting ticketing data to other systems.
agentUseSummary: Ticketbud is visible as a security-review preview. Relay will not connect while the documented beta API requires bearer access tokens in URL query strings and exposes broad attendee and mutation authority without granular scopes.

capabilities.label: Access authorized ticketing data
capabilities.description: If Ticketbud publishes a header-based, scoped and lifecycle-complete contract, expose only reviewed ticketing capabilities within the consenting account authority.

blocked.label: Send access tokens in URLs
blocked.description: Relay will not place an OAuth bearer token in a URL query string where it can be retained by request logs, intermediaries or diagnostics.

blocked.label: Expose ticket-holder and purchaser data
blocked.description: Names, emails, barcodes, QR URLs, purchase status, price, quantities and custom-form responses are not exposed.

blocked.label: Run Ticketbud mutations
blocked.description: Check-in reversal, collaboration painting, collaborator invitations and every other mutation are unavailable.

blocked.label: Run Ticketbud actions before security review
blocked.description: No beta API action is callable until Ticketbud documents secure header authentication, scopes, refresh, revocation, bounds and supported event metadata reads.

approvalProfiles.label: Security review required
approvalProfiles.description: Connection, installation and agent actions remain unavailable while the provider's beta OAuth contract sends access tokens in query strings and lacks granular authority.

runtimeSupport.description: No OpenClaw tools are callable under Ticketbud's current query-token beta contract.
No Hermes tools are callable under Ticketbud's current query-token beta contract.

providerSetup.blocker: Ticketbud's official beta API documents OAuth access and refresh tokens but requires every API call to include the access token as a URL parameter. The documented operations expose attendee/purchaser PII, barcodes, check-in mutation and collaborator invitation without scopes, revocation or a safe event-metadata-only contract.
providerSetup.nextAction: Ask Ticketbud for a production header-based OAuth contract with granular scopes, complete refresh/revocation semantics, bounded event metadata endpoints and third-party distribution terms. Re-run product and security review only after those materials are published.

evidence.supports: Ticketbud labels the API beta, documents an authorization-code exchange, two-hour access tokens and refresh tokens, but requires access_token in the URL for all API calls.

The documented API surface includes attendee names, email, barcodes, purchaser identity, prices and custom responses plus check-in, collaboration and invitation mutations, without granular scopes or a documented revocation lifecycle.
Ticketbud continues to advertise API integrations as a product capability but does not publish a newer production security contract on the official integration page.
